meta.note: A thin Monday. The two-day window largely repeats Saturday's edition, so the Claude watermark details, the Cursor acquisition and the Grok imagery case are not repeated here. What is left: one aesthetic shift, one identity, two market moves and two changes inside the model providers.

stories.title: Flaws are becoming a signal again
stories.blurb: Creative Bloq reports that digital artists are deliberately bringing imperfections back into their work as AI-generated images spread. The argument is about visible authorship, not nostalgia.

stories.title: Accessibility is not a second skill set
stories.blurb: UX Collective reframes accessibility as a translation of things designers already do rather than a separate discipline. The starting point is WebAIM's annual crawl of the top million home pages, whose 2026 results found errors on 95.9% of them.

stories.title: Pentagram builds an identity around a 13th-century roof
stories.blurb: Muziekcentrum De Bijloke in Ghent sits inside a medieval hospital founded in 1251, with an oak roof structure over a modern hall that wraps the audience around the stage. Pentagram's new identity for the venue is dynamic rather than fixed.

stories.title: The Instagram logo becomes everyone else's campaign
stories.blurb: Brands from McDonald's to ChatGPT have jumped on the new Instagram mark with their own "time for a refresh" posts. A second piece pushes back on the reflex of blaming Gen Z taste for the redesign.

stories.title: Concept art built in VR, finished in Blender
stories.blurb: Bart Tchorzewski walks through combining VR sculpting with conventional 3D modelling to build a futuristic robot figure. A process piece, not a tool announcement.

stories.title: Stripe reportedly buys the router layer
stories.blurb: TechCrunch reports Stripe is set to acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for more than $7B. OpenRouter's CEO recently described the company as Stripe for AI.

stories.title: Anthropic's CEO calls the backlash a trust problem
stories.blurb: Dario Amodei frames the current backlash against AI as fundamentally a crisis of trust, and pushes back on the claim that he has been painting an overly pessimistic picture.

stories.title: OpenAI disbands its preparedness team
stories.blurb: According to the Financial Times, OpenAI dissolved the team that assessed whether models posed serious risks and developed mitigations for them at the end of last month.

stories.title: ChatGPT starts recording how you work
stories.blurb: The macOS desktop app has a feature called Computer History that turns clicks and keystrokes into training data, builds a timeline of your activity and suggests automations or picks up unfinished tasks. ChatGPT and Codex can both read it.
